title: Friday — Entering your career
body:
Friday — Entering your career

Today's goal: run your life like a project, and turn Week 1 into something submitted.

STAR bullets — achievement bullets, not duty bullets

You get to build your story on purpose: skills, projects, evidence. The shift is duties → achievements — not "what I was responsible for" but "what I accomplished, with evidence."

STAR in one breath:

  • Context (Situation/Task): the situation and task, in one short phrase.
  • Action: a strong verb — built, analyzed, designed, led.
  • Result: the "so what?" — ideally with a number.

Bullet formula: [Power verb] + [what you did / context] + [result or benefit].

Two examples:

  • "Resolved 15+ customer issues per shift, improving satisfaction and reducing manager escalations."
  • "Built a Python script to automate file cleanup, saving ~30 minutes per week."

SMART goals — a way to turn a wish into a plan

  • Specific — exactly what you'll do.
  • Measurable — how you'll track it.
  • Achievable — challenging but possible.
  • Relevant — matters to you right now.
  • Time-bound — a deadline.

"If you can't tell when you're done, it's not a goal yet."

Pomodoro — focus sprints

Your brain starts lying when a task feels big. Pomodoro makes the first step small: 15 minutes on, 5 minutes off (build up to 25/5 with experience). One task only. Phone away, notifications off. When distracted, write it down and come back to the work — don't chase it.

The 3-2-1 CV/resume habit — tiny, repeatable

  • 3 daily notes (wins, work, learning) — a running document you keep on your phone.
  • 2 weekly paragraphs in a running CV doc, written as STAR stories.
  • 1 monthly resume bullet — a measurable achievement.

Remember: CV = your full story. Resume = your best highlights for one job. Building the CV all semester means the resume is just curation later, not a panic-write the week before you need one.

What's due today, by 4:00 PM

  • A04 — Resume: a real, current resume, using STAR bullets, not duty bullets — the 3-2-1 habit above is what makes this easy instead of a scramble.
  • A05 — Dream Job Paper: name a specific, real job you could apply for, and why it's the one you want.
  • A06 — Professional Gap Analysis: compare your current skills against that job's real requirements, and build a plan to close the gap.
  • A09 — Career Reflection: nine short, individually-graded questions — what part of that job you're eager for, what part worries you, and why it matters (see below).

A01–A03 (transcript, progress report, degree plan) were due Wednesday — if you're missing one of those, get it in too, but today's focus is these three.

About A09 — this isn't busywork

Same idea as Wednesday's A08, career side: A04–A06 prove you can build a resume and compare yourself against a real job. A09 is where you think about what that job actually means for you — separated out, individually pointed, so it doesn't get skipped. Three questions about the part of the job you're genuinely looking forward to, five working through the hardest part (name it, find three ways to prepare, pick one, name your next step, tie it to a real class or skill), and one about whether this career direction actually fits your values. Full prompts in assignments/A09_career_reflection.md.

Getting started on A05 and A06

Both ask you to get specific, not hypothetical:

  • A05 (Dream Job Paper): don't pick "something in tech" — pick an actual job posting or job title you could apply for, now or later. A real posting (search any job board in your field) gives you real requirements to write about instead of guessing.
  • A06 (Gap Analysis): use the same job you picked for A05. List what you already have (hard and soft skills) next to what the job actually asks for, and be honest about the gap — that's the point of the assignment, not a flaw in it.

Full instructions are in each assignment file — this is just enough to get you started without overthinking the target.

4:00 PM matters: it's this term's last day to add a class without special permission. Everything this week — including today's three — exists so you have real information before that door closes, not after.

Looking ahead: A07 — Advisor name and meeting time

Not due today. A07 lands later in the semester, timed to when registration for next semester opens, so the meeting happens right when you can actually act on your advisor's advice.

Exit ticket

  1. What did you submit today (A01/A02/A03)?
  2. When is your next scheduled focus sprint for this class (day/time)?
  3. What's one thing you want help with next week?
